source: Netball Skills and Conditioning Manual, Level 1, 3rd version, Niel du Plessis and Erin Burger, Catching section, page 72. The manual describes the drill as: a person passes to the person who faces to a side, placing the ball in front of the receiver; the worker, with the hand closest to the passer, tries to control the ball, pull it in and pass back to the passer; if the worker struggles the passer will use a lob pass; and if the ball cannot be caught it may be bounced to gain control. The cues are the manual's. The numeric bands are NOT, and are PROVISIONAL until a coach sets them.

checkpoints.cue: Face to the side. The ball is coming over your shoulder.
checkpoints.why: The manual has the worker facing to a side. A player who starts square is not doing this drill.

checkpoints.cue: Feet planted, knees ready. The turn comes from your trunk.
checkpoints.why: Turning by stepping is a footwork drill. This one trains the trunk to work over a still base.

checkpoints.cue: Near hand to the ball. Control it out in front.
checkpoints.why: The manual names the hand closest to the passer. Reaching with the far hand turns the shoulders too early and loses the ball.

checkpoints.cue: Still turned as you take it. Do not square up early.
checkpoints.why: Squaring up before control is what makes the ball bounce off the hands.

checkpoints.cue: Reach across your body to meet it.
checkpoints.why: The ball is placed in front of a turned athlete, so the near arm has to travel.

checkpoints.cue: Second hand on. Square up as you gather it.
checkpoints.why: One hand controls, two hands secure. The turn unwinds as the second hand arrives.

checkpoints.cue: Bring your chest round to where the pass is going.
checkpoints.why: The pass back to the passer starts from a square chest.

checkpoints.cue: Pull it in to your chest and pass back.
checkpoints.why: The manual finishes this drill with a pass back to the passer, so the ball has to be secured first.
Turning and reaching at once tempts an athlete to lean, which costs the pass that follows.
